subject.title: fix(mcp): MCP disabled: true silently ignored — gateway spawns server processes anyway

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support `disabled` as an MCP server configuration alias?
rationale: Current OpenClaw and Codex contracts define `enabled`; accepting an inverse alias introduces a new public configuration surface and precedence policy that implementation evidence alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Keep canonical `enabled`
options.body: Diagnose or migrate `disabled` when warranted while retaining one activation field in steady-state runtime.

options.title: Support both keys
options.body: Declare and document `disabled` across all configuration surfaces with precedence, upgrade coverage, and real runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical `enabled`
recommendation.body: Diagnose or migrate `disabled` when warranted while retaining one activation field in steady-state runtime.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current MCP normalization and canonical activation handling in the central files.
